thread:
Liz (Design): quick sync — thinking about a compact histogram for the 'request latency' card. main concerns: bin count heuristics, label density, and keyboard/voiceover navigation. attaching mock in Figma (link).
Ranjit (Data Viz): +1. main UX tradeoff is bin adaptivity vs comparability across charts. if bins change per time window, it confuses trend comparisons.
Sam (Frontend): is the plan to keep a fixed bucket count (e.g., 20) and adjust bucket width, or keep width fixed and vary count? performance matters for streaming data.
Ranjit (Data Viz): prefer fixed bucket count and variable width. simpler delta encoding for hover tooltips. recommendation: default 16 bins, fallback to 8 on tiny widths.
Liz (Design): 16 default sounds good. visual density: do we show x-axis ticks for each bucket or sampled ticks? worried about label collisions in compact mode.
Courtney (A11y): from a11y POV, buckets need exposed labels via aria-label on the bars and keyboard focus order. swipe gestures for VoiceOver should move by bucket, not by pixel.
Sam (Frontend): implementation note: we can render as <rect> per bucket and set tabindex=0 on each. but that could be 100s of elements for long time ranges.
Ranjit (Data Viz): true — we should clamp interactive buckets to a max of 60. beyond that we aggregate into an "other" bucket or enable a dense mode with summarised interactions.
Liz (Design): what about hover vs click on mobile? mobile users expect tapping a bar reveals a mini tooltip with count and percentage.
Courtney (A11y): for screen readers, expose an overall summary first: "Histogram of request latency: 16 buckets, median 120ms, 3% > 1s" then allow arrow-key navigation per bucket. For VoiceOver swipe right/left we should map to next semantic bucket.
Sam (Frontend): mapping swipe to buckets could be implemented with a virtualized list of bucket descriptors and a single focusable container that updates aria-live on swipe.
DesignBot: accessibility checklist: ensure each bucket has aria-label, role="button" or "listitem" as appropriate, provide aria-roledescription="histogram bucket".
Ranjit (Data Viz): microcopy: bucket label format should be "50–100 ms (12.3%)" not "50–100ms: 12.3" — clearer for voice.
Liz (Design): agree. also propose a subtle outline on keyboard focus and a 2px darker border to show focus when compact (so it remains visible at small sizes).
Sam (Frontend): will prototype with SVG rects + focus ring. question: do we show axis ticks at bucket boundaries or only show min/median/max annotations to save space?
Liz (Design): prefer min/median/max with small inline icons for median. keep x-axis labels minimal in compact mode.
Courtney (A11y): include a visually-hidden summary of the axis scale: "x-axis: 0ms to 2000ms" for screen readers.
Ranjit (Data Viz): outlier handling: currently long-tail spikes wreck bin distribution. suggestion: offer an optional "cap" toggle that groups > p95 into a single overflow bucket labeled ">= 1s".
Liz (Design): nice — add microcopy tooltip on the cap toggle: "Group extreme latencies to preserve histogram shape." keep default off but recommend turning on for noisy endpoints.
Sam (Frontend): sounds doable. will add config: { "bins": 16, "overflowCap": "p95", "compactMode": true }
Ranjit (Data Viz): one more: when users zoom or change time range, keep bucket count stable to avoid janky visual jumps. animate width changes instead of remapping indexes.
Liz (Design): agreed. final requests: keyboard focus style, aria-live summary on focus change, overflow cap microcopy, and sampled axis labels. I'll update the mock and post back.
Sam (Frontend): I'll queue an implementation spike and share a demo link once ready. thanks!
Courtney (A11y): I'll draft the SR labels and test with VoiceOver gestures once demo is up. :thumbsup:
Liz (Design): thanks team — moving to comments on the Figma file now.
